items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: Yeah. But he didn't come out and jam too much, because he was... You know, he was a big money man.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Well, the main place where most of the musicians would hang out in California was Jack's. Like, all the saxophone players, Wardell and Dexter and Teddy Edwards and so forth, would hang out down there. But they had Art Tatum up at Lovejoy's, and somebody else used to go hang up there, too... Besides Garner. I mean...
What about Nat King Cole? He was around there, too, wasn't he, at different times?

Yeah. But he didn't come out and jam too much, because he was... You know, he was a big money man. He couldn't afford to be seen out in them after-hour joints and so forth. So he was making his money the other way. But as far as I can tell you about the sessions, the greatest sessions that I heard out there were at Jack's. You know, there were a lot of saxophone players that used to play there, and I'd go and jam sometimes with them.
